fields.title: Moka Decathlon Night Run 2026
fields.short_description: The Moka Decathlon Night Run 2026 is a highly popular 10 km night-time road race held in Moka, Mauritius, featuring 2,700 runners navigating a vibrant, music-filled, and illuminated urban course.
fields.description:
The Moka Decathlon Night Run returns for its 5th edition on Saturday, 21 November 2026, transforming the heart of Moka Smart City into a massive outdoor sporting celebration. Starting at 19:30 from the scenic Telfair Amphitheatre, the event blends competitive road running with a high-energy festival atmosphere, featuring live DJ stations, light animations, and cheering zones lining the streets.
The challenging 10 km course tests participants with a mix of steady climbs through Helvétia, fast straights down the A7 road, and a technical loop near Bagatelle before heading back for a grand finish at the Telfair race village. Open to runners of all levels aged 12 and up, the event is heavily integrated with the local community and stands out as a flagship night race in Mauritius, with all 2,700 registrations fully booked a month in advance.
fields.itinerary_text:
• 18:00 – Race Village Opens: Runners arrive at Telfair La Promenade to park, drop off bags, and soak up the pre-race atmosphere.
• 18:45 – Warm-Up Session: A high-energy, guided dynamic warm-up begins near the Telfair Amphitheatre stage.
• 19:15 – Starting Line Line-up: Participants gather at the starting corrals as the final race briefing is given.
• 19:30 – Race Start: The horn blows and 2,700 runners head out into the illuminated streets of Moka.
• 20:00 – Bagatelle Hydration Point: Leading runners hit the halfway refreshment station at kilometer 5.5 near Decathlon Bagatelle.
• 20:15 – First Finishers Arrive: The top athletes cross the finish line back at Telfair to live music and cheering crowds.
• 21:00 – Podium Ceremony & After-Party: Official awards are presented to the winners, followed by a festive post-race celebration in the race village.

fields.title: Ebony Forest Reserve
fields.short_description: Endemic tree canopy restoration and bird watching
fields.itinerary_text: Located in the southwestern highlands, this reserve protects some of the island's last remaining primary ebony forest. Options include self-guided canopy walkway tours, guided plant-a-tree experiences, and open-air 4x4 safari tours centered on biodiversity protection.

fields.title: La Vallée de Ferney Guided Eco-Walk
fields.short_description: Forest protection and rewilding.
fields.itinerary_text: A 200-hectare nature sanctuary in the Bambou Mountain range dedicated to preserving indigenous flora and fauna. Guided tours take you along nature trails where you can witness the feeding of the endangered Mauritius Kestrel (the island's native falcon) and see endemic plants like the Ebony tree.
